title: Turning a container into display:flex blockifies its direct child — the new block box intercepts descendants' height:100% chains and collapses them to auto
trigger: After setting display:flex (column) on a shell element, a descendant that used height:100% (e.g. a video styled by the site to fill its player) collapses to content height — dead bands appear inside the shell even though the shell itself keeps its height
principle: Percentage heights resolve against the nearest ancestor with a definite height — and for in-flow elements, only block-level ancestors count; inline ancestors (framework host elements like Angular's <app-watch>) are skipped. Before flexing the shell, a descendant's height:100% could skip those inline wrappers and resolve against the shell directly. Once the shell is display:flex, its direct child is blockified into a containing block — now it intercepts the chain but computes to auto → everything below collapses. Re-link the chain by pinning height:100% (and display:block so inlines honor it) on every element between the shell and the video; a % that resolves to a definite value makes the next level's % resolvable, so the chain propagates all the way down.

cases.context: kisskh desktop: .col-12 shell (stretched to row height 736px) > APP-WATCH > MAT-VIDEO > .videoplayer{height:100%} > video. Natively .videoplayer skips the inline ancestors and takes .col-12's height → video fills the column. After split view set .col-12 to display:flex column, APP-WATCH blockified and .videoplayer collapsed 736→287 — video floated mid-stage with ~440px dead space.
cases.bad:
playerShell.style.display = 'flex'; playerShell.style.flexDirection = 'column';
// descendants' height:100% now hit a blockified auto-height flex item

applyFor: Restructuring any element to display:flex/absolute when descendants rely on percentage heights
